entities.name: Urodilatin
observations: At 0.05 μM during the first 15 minutes of reperfusion, improved functional recovery and reduced biochemical and histologic injury in isolated rat hearts.
Protection was concentration-dependent: 0.01 μM was ineffective and 1 μM was not beneficial.

entities.name: PMID:10728355
observations: In isolated rat hearts subjected to 40 or 60 minutes of no-flow ischemia and 2 hours of reperfusion, 0.05 μM urodilatin during the first 15 minutes of reperfusion improved contractile recovery after 40-minute ischemia and reduced LV end-diastolic pressure, LDH release, and contraction-band necrosis after 60-minute ischemia.
Urodilatin attenuated reperfusion-associated myocardial cGMP depletion.

entities.name: PMID:11476750
observations: In isolated rat hearts, 0.05 μM urodilatin during the first 15 minutes of reperfusion improved functional recovery and reduced peak LDH release by 40%; 0.01 μM was ineffective and 1 μM produced no benefit.
The protective effect was abolished by ANP-receptor inhibition.

entities.name: Urodilatin reperfusion protection
observations: Urodilatin limited acute ischemia–reperfusion injury in isolated rat hearts when administered early during reperfusion, with benefit demonstrated by functional, biochemical, and histologic endpoints at 0.05 μM.
